info.title: DND Campaign Vault Server API
info.description:
Comprehensive OpenAPI documentation for the DND Campaign Vault API.

Notes:
- Request/response envelopes follow `{ data, error }`.
- Operations may use the existing session cookie or a scoped bearer API key (`Authorization: Bearer <key>`).
- Bearer keys are subject to the owner's current campaign access and the key's resource permissions.
- The stateless MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint is available at `/mcp` on this same server; it exposes only the named operations documented in `docs/AgentIntegration.md`. The API remains the authorization and business-logic authority.

get.description: Auto-documented from server route `artifacts/[artifactId].get.ts`. This operation uses the project standard API envelope `{ data, error }`.

Streams a private artifact after read access is verified. A storage adapter with range support serves one valid `Range` request as 206; otherwise the complete artifact is returned. Malformed or multiple ranges deliberately fall back to 200. Starts beyond the artifact, reversed ranges, zero-length suffixes, and unsafe integer values return 416. Oversized valid ends are clamped to the artifact size.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: One byte range for media seeking, for example `bytes=0-1023` or `bytes=-1024`. It is ignored when storage does not support range reads.

200.description: Complete binary artifact with the artifact's stored MIME type. This is also returned for missing, malformed, or multiple Range values, and when storage cannot range-read.

Accept-Ranges.description: Present with `bytes` when the storage adapter supports range reads.

Content-Length.description: Present when the storage adapter reports the complete artifact size.

206.description: Requested single byte range as a binary artifact.

Content-Range.description: The byte interval served and the full artifact size.

Content-Length.description: The number of bytes in the partial response.

416.description: The requested byte range cannot be satisfied. The response is the standard JSON API error envelope, not an artifact stream.

Content-Range.description: The complete artifact size, expressed as an unsatisfied byte range.

get.description: Read current encounter state and role-aware availableActions. Selection is local UI state and does not change the turn.

200.description: Updated encounter state, including phase, participants, conditions, history, activeParticipantId, and availableActions with reasons.

patch.description: Update metadata in Planned/Active/Paused, or execute a typed lifecycle action. start: Planned with participants; pause: Active; resume: Paused with participants; complete: Active/Paused; abandon: Planned/Active/Paused; reopen: Completed/Abandoned to Paused, preserving state; reset: Active/Paused to Planned, resetting round/turn only. Raw status/currentRound/currentTurnIndex updates are rejected. Invalid phases return 409 ENCOUNTER_ACTION_UNAVAILABLE.

200.description: Updated encounter state, including phase, participants, conditions, history, activeParticipantId, and availableActions with reasons.

get.description: Auto-documented from server route `encounters/[encounterId]/combatants/index.get.ts`. This operation uses the project standard API envelope `{ data, error }`.

post.description: Creates a combatant, filling omitted HP, armorClass, and speed from its campaign-linked character sheet or saved stat block. Glossary sources use an unambiguous linked character sheet. Explicit values (including zero) win; saved stat-block values take precedence over character defaults. Explicit maxHp initializes omitted currentHp; otherwise source current HP or default max HP is used. Missing stats remain unset. Uses the standard API envelope `{ data, error }`. Planned/Active/Paused only. Batch {participants:[...]} accepts 1â€“50 entries atomically and returns full encounter state; legacy single input returns the created participant. No partial batch writes. Planned/Active/Paused only. Batch {participants:[...]} accepts 1â€“50 entries atomically and returns full encounter state; legacy single input returns the created participant. No partial batch writes.

200.description: Batch: full encounter state. Single input: created combatant in the standard envelope.

patch.description: Damage/healing requires Active/Paused and known current HP. Conditions may be prepared in Planned and edited in Active/Paused. All target ids must belong to the encounter; duplicate or invalid targets reject the whole batch. Numeric amounts are integers 1â€“9999. Finished encounters are read-only until reopened.

200.description: Updated encounter state, including phase, participants, conditions, history, activeParticipantId, and availableActions with reasons.

404.description: Encounter or target inaccessible; nothing changed.

Streams a shared recap after public campaign and recap access are checked. Storage with range support serves one valid byte range for seeking and playback resume. Malformed or multiple ranges deliberately fall back to the complete 200 response; starts beyond the artifact, reversed ranges, zero-length suffixes, and unsafe integer values return 416. Oversized valid ends are clamped to the artifact size.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: One byte range, for example `bytes=0-1023` or `bytes=-1024`. It is ignored when storage does not support range reads.

Content-Length.description: The number of bytes in the partial response.

416.description: The requested byte range cannot be satisfied. Public recap streaming returns an empty response body for this status.

post.summary: Call the stateless MCP Streamable HTTP endpoint
post.description: Send an MCP JSON-RPC request with a scoped bearer API key. Uses JSON responses and no server-side MCP session. An Origin header, when present, must match the configured public application origin. Campaign tool calls retain REST campaign and resource authorization. The dice_roll tool accepts a notation string (1-200 characters) and optional mode: normal (default), advantage, or disadvantage. Normal mode returns notation, mode, terms with individual dice and signed subtotals, and total. Advantage/disadvantage require a single d20 with an optional integer modifier (e.g. d20+5) and return notation, mode, both dice in rolls, selectedRoll, modifier, and total with the modifier applied once. It uses the shared dice roller and requires only a valid API key. Agents should prefer it over inventing roll results. Rolls are not persisted.

200.description: MCP JSON-RPC result or protocol error

401.description: Missing, invalid, expired, or revoked bearer key

406.description: Client must accept application/json and text/event-stream

500.description: MCP request could not be processed
